name: goth-provider-scoped-token-credential-negotiation
instr:
Applications using Goth can choose token-endpoint credential placement per provider instead of mutating process-wide OAuth2 behavior. Kakao, Meetup, and WePay support Basic-header, form-parameter, and ordered automatic negotiation while exposing structured diagnostics through direct operations and Gothic callbacks. Existing authorization URLs, session formats, callback lifecycle, refresh behavior, profile inputs, and successful example output remain compatible.

Every configured policy is validated before network activity, and automatic negotiation follows its declared order only until a valid token response succeeds. Each operation produces immutable `TokenAuthEvidence` containing ordered `TokenAuthAttempt` values and terminal classification, without credentials, authorization codes, or tokens. Failures use `TokenAuthError`, preserve the underlying transport, decoding, or endpoint error through `Error`, `Unwrap`, and `Evidence`, and carry the same sanitized evidence observed by callers. Registry publication, replacement, lookup through `GetTokenAuthPolicy` and `GetTokenAuthEvidence`, and clearing are atomic and isolate policy and evidence by provider. Kakao, Meetup, and WePay mutate sessions only after successful validation, while Meetup applies one policy to callbacks, `RefreshToken`, and `RefreshTokenWithEvidence`.
